newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algiers bomb kills five, two defused - newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Algiers bomb kills five, two defused - newspapers.

text.p: A bomb blast outside an Algiers high school killed five teenagers and security forces defused two other bombs in the centre of the capital, Algerian newspaper said on Wednesday.

The bomb outside Frantz Fanon high school in downtown Algiers killed five school children on Tuesday and wounded 32 other people, including six badly injured, said the usually well-informed El Watan daily.
Algerian security forces said the blast killed three schoolgirls, a 12-year-old boy and wounded 21 other people.
"According to bomb disposal experts, two other bombs set to explode at the same time were defused at Audin place and outside Bab el Oued town hall," said La Tribune newspaper.
The bomb went off outside the school, in the working class Bab el Oued district, at lunch hour. The area is near the Casbah and a militant Moslem hotbed.
There was no claim of responsibility.

About 50,000 people have died in the strife between Moslem rebels and the government since 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had a huge lead. Algeria is to hold parliamentary elections on June 5 from which radical Islamists are barred.
